issues.problem: The left boundary accepts an opener ( [ < " ' that sits inside a larger non-whitespace token, provided the character before the opener is not alphanumeric. A closer ends a token even when the host continues after it. Path dot segments are not rejected. So a vendor URL credits in five cases: (Q) as a query, fragment or path value of another URL when it is wrapped in a delimiter; (J) inside javascript: or data: URLs; (L) in Markdown link text when the text contains a space, in [..][ref] labels, in link titles, in HTML title attributes and in HTML anchor text; (C) before a host continuation behind ' " ` ) ] < > or an invisible control character that Python treats as whitespace (\x1c-\x1f); (P) with ../ traversal on path-prefix packs. This is the same 'value inside another URL' and 'link text pointing elsewhere' attack that r9 asked to close. The plain form '?next=https://cursor.com/x' is rejected, but '?next=(https://cursor.com/x)' credits.

issues.suggested_fix: The token must start at the start of the text or after ASCII whitespace. Leading openers are allowed only when the whole opener run starts there, or when the opener is the '(' of a Markdown '](' target. Cut the token only at ASCII whitespace or closers, and keep \x1c-\x1f and Unicode spaces inside it, so non-ASCII and control characters reject it. After a closer, only closers or trailing punctuation may follow, and then whitespace or the end of the text. Skip any candidate whose opener run contains '['. Skip quoted candidates inside a '](target "title")'. Reject a path with a '.' or '..' segment (check before the trailing-punctuation strip).
